title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 15
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Five hospitals:

Ashcombe: 240 beds, 88% occupancy, average stay 4.2 days
Brentwell: 410 beds, 92% occupancy, average stay 6.8 days
Cadmore: 150 beds, 79% occupancy, average stay 2.4 days
Derringham: 620 beds, 81% occupancy, average stay 5.5 days
Eastholt: 300 beds, 84% occupancy, average stay 4.9 days

Which hospital treats the most patients per bed in a year?
questions.explanation: A bed treats 365 days of occupancy divided by the average stay: Ashcombe 76, Brentwell 49, Cadmore 120, Derringham 54, Eastholt 63. Cadmore leads at about 120, because its patients leave after 2.4 days. Brentwell has the highest occupancy at 92% and Derringham treats the most patients outright, but a bed that is full of the same patient for a week turns over slowly.

questions.prompt:
Annual figures:

2018: 480
2019: 512
2020: 445
2021: 503
2022: 561
2023: 598
2024: 636

What was the average change per year over the whole period?
questions.explanation: The figure rose from 480 to 636, a change of 156 spread over 6 intervals between 7 readings: 26 a year. Dividing by 7 rather than 6 gives 22.29 — the classic error of counting readings instead of the gaps between them. The path was not steady: 2020 fell before the run of rises resumed.

questions.prompt:
Units sold by channel:

Retail: 1,200 in 2020, 1,560 in 2024
Trade: 1,600 in 2020, 4,200 in 2024
Online: 400 in 2020, 2,300 in 2024
Other: 800 in 2020, 650 in 2024

Which channel grew most as a share of the total?
options: E. All four grew by the same share
questions.explanation: Totals were 4,000 and 8,710, so shares moved: Retail 30.0% to 17.9%, Trade 40.0% to 48.2%, Online 10.0% to 26.4%, Other 20.0% to 7.5%. Online gains 16.4 points, the most of any channel. Trade added more units — 2,600 against 1,900 — but the total grew underneath it, so its share rose by less.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 18, 21, 21, 24, 27, 30, 34

Every reading is then increased by 5. Which statement about the effect is accurate?
options: A. Every measure of the set rises by 5
C. The mean rises by 5 but the median does not
E. The mean, the median and the mode each rise by 5, and the range is unchanged
questions.explanation: Before: mean 25, median 24, mode 21, range 16. After: mean 30, median 29, mode 26, range 16. Shifting every value moves anything that names a position in the data, but the gaps between the values are untouched — which is why the range stands still and "every measure rises" is wrong.

questions.prompt:
A hall costs GBP 280.00 to hire, plus GBP 14.00 a head for catering. Tickets sell at GBP 25.00.

Select the smallest number of tickets that covers the costs AND the profit at that number.
options: E. The event cannot cover its costs at any number of tickets
questions.explanation: Each ticket contributes GBP 25.00 − GBP 14.00 = GBP 11.00 towards the hire, so covering GBP 280.00 needs GBP 280.00 / GBP 11.00 = 25.45 tickets — 26 once rounded up. At 26: takings GBP 650.00 against costs GBP 644.00, a profit of GBP 6.00. At 25 the event is still GBP 5.00 short.

questions.prompt:
An item lists at GBP 480.00. A 15% trade discount is applied, and a 5% rebate is then taken off the discounted price.

Select the final price AND the single discount that would have the same effect.
questions.explanation: The trade discount leaves GBP 408.00, and the rebate takes GBP 20.40 off that: GBP 387.60. The buyer pays 80.75% of the list price, so the equivalent single discount is 19.25%. Adding the two percentages gives 20%, which charges the rebate against the full list price rather than the discounted one.

questions.prompt:
Two mailings:

Mailing One: 4,800 sent, 384 replies
Mailing Two: 22,000 sent, 1,320 replies

Select the mailing with the higher response rate AND the mailing that brought in more replies.
options: A. Mailing One on both measures
B. Mailing Two on both measures
C. Mailing Two on the response rate; Mailing One on replies
D. Mailing One on the response rate; Mailing Two on replies
E. The two mailings are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Response rates: Mailing One 8.0%, Mailing Two 6.0%. Replies: Mailing One 384, Mailing Two 1,320. The better-targeted mailing went to less than a quarter as many people, so the higher rate does not bring in the higher count.

questions.prompt:
Supplier A quotes 4,250 euros and Supplier B quotes GBP 3,780.00. The rate is 1.14 euros to the pound.

Select Supplier A's price in sterling AND the cheaper of the two suppliers.
options: A. GBP 3,728.07; Supplier A is cheaper
B. GBP 4,845.00; Supplier B is cheaper
C. GBP 3,728.07; Supplier B is cheaper
D. GBP 3,728.07; the two quotes are equal
E. GBP 4,845.00; Supplier A is cheaper
questions.explanation: Euros convert to pounds by dividing: 4,250 / 1.14 = GBP 3,728.07, which undercuts Supplier B's GBP 3,780.00 by GBP 51.93. Multiplying by the rate instead gives GBP 4,845.00, a figure larger than the euro total, which cannot be right when a pound is worth more than a euro.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): potholes repaired — Council P 2,400, Council Q 1,150, Council R 4,900

SOURCE 2 (table): road network — Council P 800 km, Council Q 230 km, Council R 1,400 km

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The commendation goes to the council repairing the most potholes for each kilometre of road it maintains."

Which council is commended?
options: C. The three councils are equal
D. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Repairs divided by road length: Council P 3 a kilometre, Council Q 5 a kilometre, Council R 3.5 a kilometre. Council Q leads and has much the smallest network. Council R repaired 4,900 potholes, more than twice as many, across 1,400 km of road.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Sales per employee fell from GBP 142,000.00 to GBP 118,000.00."

SOURCE 2 (table): headcount rose from 90 to 145.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board wants to know what happened to total sales."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Total sales fell by about 17%
B. Total sales rose by about 34%, because headcount grew faster than sales per head fell
C. Each employee worked less hard than before
E. Total sales cannot be worked out from these sources
questions.explanation: Total sales are headcount multiplied by sales per employee: before, 90 × GBP 142,000.00 = GBP 12,780,000.00; after, 145 × GBP 118,000.00 = GBP 17,110,000.00 — a rise of about 34%. The per-head figure fell because the denominator grew by 61% while the numerator grew by less, which says nothing about how hard anyone worked.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): bids received — Bidder A GBP 96,400.00, Bidder B GBP 108,900.00, Bidder C GBP 102,300.00

SOURCE 2 (note): Bidder A is a subsidiary of the incumbent supplier, and the tender rules bar any bid from a connected party.

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Award the contract to the lowest compliant bid."

Which bidder wins the contract?
options: D. The contract cannot be awarded
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Bidder A bids GBP 96,400.00, the lowest of the three, but source 2 disqualifies it outright, so its price never comes into it. Of the compliant bids, Bidder B at GBP 108,900.00 and Bidder C at GBP 102,300.00, Bidder C is lower by GBP 6,600.00. Eligibility is settled before price.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): the branch took GBP 412,000 last year.

SOURCE 2 (memo): "Every branch carries a target of GBP 400,000 for the year."

SOURCE 3 (email): "Head office wants a yes or no: did the branch meet its target?"

Which source or sources are needed to answer head office?
options: C. Sources 1 and 2 together; neither settles it alone
E. The question cannot be answered even with all three sources
questions.explanation: Source 1 gives a figure with nothing to measure it against, and source 2 gives a bar with no figure to compare to it. Put together they answer the question: GBP 412,000 clears GBP 400,000 by GBP 12,000, so the answer is yes. Source 3 only poses the question and adds no information.

questions.prompt:
How old is Ravi?

(1) Ravi is 6 years older than Sam.
(2) The ages of Ravi and Sam add to 34.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) ties the two ages together but fixes neither, and (2) fixes their total but not the split. Together, Sam is (34 − 6) / 2 = 14 and Ravi is 20. Each statement supplies exactly one of the two facts the answer needs.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of the positive integer x?

(1) x is a factor of 24.
(2) x is even.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24, so (1) leaves eight candidates and (2) alone leaves every even number. Together they leave 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 — six values, not one. The statements narrow the field without closing it.

questions.prompt:
What is the area of a triangle?

(1) Its base is 10 cm and the perpendicular height to that base is 6 cm.
(2) Two of its sides measure 10 cm and 6 cm.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) is the area formula in words: half of 10 times 6 is 30 square centimetres. (2) gives two lengths but no angle between them, so the triangle could be almost flat or nearly right-angled, with areas anywhere from close to zero up to 30. A right angle between those two sides would satisfy both statements at once.

questions.prompt:
What is the 10th term of an arithmetic sequence?

(1) The first term is 4 and the common difference is 3.
(2) The 4th term is 13 and the 7th term is 22.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1) the 10th term is 4 + 9 × 3 = 31. From (2) three steps carry the sequence from 13 to 22, so the common difference is 3, the first term is 4, and the 10th term is 31 again. The two statements describe the same sequence, so either alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt:
Which farm produces the most tonnes in a year?

Farm | Hectares | Yield (tonnes a hectare) | Price a tonne | Irrigated
Ashfold | 340 | 8.2 | GBP 185.00 | 40%
Barrowden | 120 | 11.6 | GBP 210.00 | 85%
Calderfield | 580 | 6.4 | GBP 172.00 | 20%
Dunsley | 260 | 9.1 | GBP 198.00 | 30%
Edgeworth | 450 | 7.3 | GBP 205.00 | 35%
Fenniscliffe | 90 | 12.4 | GBP 225.00 | 95%
questions.explanation: Tonnage is hectares multiplied by yield: Ashfold 2,788, Barrowden 1,392, Calderfield 3,712, Dunsley 2,366, Edgeworth 3,285, Fenniscliffe 1,116. Calderfield produces the most on the worst yield in the table, 6.4 tonnes a hectare, simply by farming 580 of them. Fenniscliffe gets 12.4 tonnes from every hectare but has only 90.

questions.prompt:
Which farm earns the most from its crop in a year?

Farm | Hectares | Yield (tonnes a hectare) | Price a tonne | Irrigated
Ashfold | 340 | 8.2 | GBP 185.00 | 40%
Barrowden | 120 | 11.6 | GBP 210.00 | 85%
Calderfield | 580 | 6.4 | GBP 172.00 | 20%
Dunsley | 260 | 9.1 | GBP 198.00 | 30%
Edgeworth | 450 | 7.3 | GBP 205.00 | 35%
Fenniscliffe | 90 | 12.4 | GBP 225.00 | 95%
questions.explanation: Revenue is tonnage multiplied by the price a tonne: Ashfold GBP 515,780.00, Barrowden GBP 292,320.00, Calderfield GBP 638,464.00, Dunsley GBP 468,468.00, Edgeworth GBP 673,425.00, Fenniscliffe GBP 251,100.00. Edgeworth earns the most despite Calderfield growing 427 more tonnes, because it sells at GBP 205.00 against GBP 172.00.

questions.prompt:
How many farms are above the median on both yield and the share of land irrigated?

Farm | Hectares | Yield (tonnes a hectare) | Price a tonne | Irrigated
Ashfold | 340 | 8.2 | GBP 185.00 | 40%
Barrowden | 120 | 11.6 | GBP 210.00 | 85%
Calderfield | 580 | 6.4 | GBP 172.00 | 20%
Dunsley | 260 | 9.1 | GBP 198.00 | 30%
Edgeworth | 450 | 7.3 | GBP 205.00 | 35%
Fenniscliffe | 90 | 12.4 | GBP 225.00 | 95%
questions.explanation: The medians are 8.65 tonnes a hectare and 37.5% irrigated. Above on yield: Barrowden, Dunsley, Fenniscliffe. Above on irrigation: Ashfold, Barrowden, Fenniscliffe. On both: Barrowden and Fenniscliffe — 2. Watering the land and getting a good yield go together at the top of the table, but not everywhere in it.

questions.prompt:
Which farm earns the most from each hectare it farms?

Farm | Hectares | Yield (tonnes a hectare) | Price a tonne | Irrigated
Ashfold | 340 | 8.2 | GBP 185.00 | 40%
Barrowden | 120 | 11.6 | GBP 210.00 | 85%
Calderfield | 580 | 6.4 | GBP 172.00 | 20%
Dunsley | 260 | 9.1 | GBP 198.00 | 30%
Edgeworth | 450 | 7.3 | GBP 205.00 | 35%
Fenniscliffe | 90 | 12.4 | GBP 225.00 | 95%
questions.explanation: Revenue a hectare is yield multiplied by price: Ashfold GBP 1,517.00, Barrowden GBP 2,436.00, Calderfield GBP 1,100.80, Dunsley GBP 1,801.80, Edgeworth GBP 1,496.50, Fenniscliffe GBP 2,790.00. Fenniscliffe leads at GBP 2,790.00 and is the smallest farm in the table at 90 hectares. Edgeworth earns the most in total and Calderfield farms the most land, but neither works its ground as hard.
